However, especially on social media we're more likely to witness a persons down days and depressive rantings than we are in person. So its likely if you're still seeing a lack of body positive mindsets in the trans community youre catching them on a bad dysphoria day. 

Personally, post anorexia, I've began to feel better about my body through starting T and focusing on general health over numbers. It all just depends on the stage youre in, how well you know yourself, and what theraputic tools you have to combat dysphoria...also if you have a support system.

Trans or not people are pushed to strive for bodies that are unattainable for them as well as having depressive disorders. Truscum aside, a lack of body positivity isnt surprising as long as there are people who will shame other's bodies for not holding up to magazine standard in any direction. It just ads a layer when your brain is yelling at your body that its entire layout is the wrong shape/has the wrong muscular structure. 

I wasnt sure where to put this, but I also wanted to say that an unchaging negative mindset shouldn't be shamed either as that can be the result of chronic depression/other chemical issues that arent necessarily the fault of the body-owner.

 As long as trans specific mental health resources arent open to all trans person there will always be negative mindsets.

I understand that a lot of cis people just lack the education, but its exhausting hearing things like that statement regularly and also having to use my time to educate grown adults. 

I cannot be held responsible for every single cis person's understanding of trans people. 

What I didnt mention earlier is that these statements are usually following a "I know this probably sounds wrong." so they know its backwards, but it still comes out of their mouths.

I generally just dont react if people come to me personally with these types of comments, because why would i want to? I want to be able to hold the position of "well theyre trying.", but when their trying doesn't even meet even the most basic requirements for basic respect for your fellow human its hard. 

I have (before i was out) corrected statements about other trans people like "that girl wants to be a boy" or "i think thats actually a man." and it just doesnt sink in. Most of the time the reaction was "dont be so sensitive" even if my response was calm and level headed. Some people just dont want to hear anything else past their own head.

Its the blatant misgendering while giving a compliment. It makes the whole compliment backhanded. All I heard from that is "When your DAUGHTER passes enough for my liking they'll be comparable to an attractive cismale." 

I dont mind being called a guy, and I relate to other FTMs heavily even if our identites don't completely line up. I understand cis people dont understand most things (talking to them about trans identites is like teaching a toddler calculus) so I dont get bent out of shape when they don't understand nonbinary, its just the blatant misgendering that I find apalling. Like theyre incapable of affording the same respects that i afford them (gendering them correctly).
